prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a sideswipe while changing lanes claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1287; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following report of sideswipe collision during lane change on the interstate. Reporting party states the other vehicle drifted into their lane without signaling. Both drivers reported as uninjured at scene except the claimant, who reports wrist pain. Police report requested; file set to bodily injury review.

Entry 2: Spoke with claimant by phone. Claimant confirmed they are not represented by an attorney and is handling the claim directly. Claimant describes falling on outstretched arm after the impact and was taken to urgent care, where x-rays showed a fracture of the wrist. Medical records authorization sent to claimant for signature.

Entry 3: Received police report. Responding officer noted the other driver admitted to not checking the blind spot before moving over. Witness statement obtained from a passenger in the other vehicle, consistent with the insured driver's account. Liability assessment leaning toward the other driver at a high percentage pending final review.

Entry 4: Claimant returned signed medical authorization. Orthopedic follow-up noted a closed fracture requiring a splint and a referral for possible physical therapy. Treating physician estimates a recovery period of several weeks. Claimant asked what to expect regarding the settlement process; explained general steps and that no offer will be made until medical treatment is documented as complete.

Entry 5: Vehicle damage appraisal completed on the claimant's car, showing repairable rear-quarter panel damage. Repair estimate sent to the claimant's chosen shop. Bodily injury file remains open pending updated medical records and a final treatment summary. Follow-up call scheduled to check on claimant's recovery and document any new expenses.
